definitions.gloss: to depict; to describe; to portray (in words, art, or film)
definitions.explanation: To represent something vividly through writing, painting, film, or other artistic media. Focuses on detailed, vivid representation rather than simple explanation.

examples.japanese: {風景|ふうけい}を{描写|びょうしゃ}する。
この{小説|しょうせつ}は{戦争|せんそう}の{悲惨|ひさん}さを{描写|びょうしゃ}している。
examples.english: This novel depicts the tragedy of war.

examples.japanese: {登場人物|とうじょうじんぶつ}の{心理|しんり}を{細|こま}かく{描写|びょうしゃ}するのがこの{作家|さっか}の{特徴|とくちょう}だ。
examples.english: It is characteristic of this author to describe the psychology of characters in fine detail.

notes:
A する-verb from {描写|びょうしゃ}, a compound of {描|びょう} (depict, draw) and {写|しゃ} (copy, capture). A key term in literary criticism, art, and film studies. Emphasizes vivid, detailed representation rather than simple description.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive — takes を to mark the thing being depicted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心理|しんり}{描写|びょうしゃ} — psychological portrayal
- {情景|じょうけい}{描写|びょうしゃ} — scene description
- {人物|じんぶつ}{描写|びょうしゃ} — character portrayal
- {写実的|しゃじつてき}な{描写|びょうしゃ} — realistic depiction
- {描写力|びょうしゃりょく} — descriptive power

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {表現|ひょうげん}する — to express (broader, not limited to vivid representation)
- {描|えが}く — to draw, to depict (native Japanese, also used figuratively)
- {記述|きじゅつ}する — to describe in writing (more factual, less artistic)
